passages.text: SUN, in astronomy, a great globe of fire placed in the centre of our system, round which the earth and all the other planets revolve.
The diameter of the sun is about 883,000 miles, and its bulk exceeds that of the earth more than a million of times.
Its mean distance from the earth, as deduced from the late transits of Venus, is about 95 millions of miles.
By the motion of the spots across its disk it is found to turn round its axis in about 25 days and a half, from west to east.

Dr Herschel supposes the sun to be a solid opaque body, like the earth, surrounded by a luminous atmosphere; and the spots, according to him, are openings in this shining atmosphere, through which we see the dark body of the sun below.
He even thinks it probable that the body of the sun is inhabited, like the planets, the lower clouds of its atmosphere shielding the inhabitants from the glare above.
How the sun supplies its prodigious waste of light and heat is not known. Sir Isaac Newton conjectured that comets, falling at length into the sun, may serve to recruit its fire.
The Sun is the star at the centre of the Solar System. It is a nearly perfect sphere of hot plasma, and it is by far the most important source of light and heat for life on Earth.

The Sun's diameter is about 1.39 million kilometres (about 864,000 miles), about 109 times that of Earth. Its volume could hold about 1.3 million Earths, and it contains about 99.86 percent of the mass of the Solar System.

The mean distance from Earth to the Sun is about 150 million kilometres, or about 93 million miles. This distance is called the astronomical unit. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
The Sun does not rotate as a solid body. Its equator turns once in about 25 days, while regions near the poles take about 35 days.
The Sun has no solid surface. It is made of hot plasma, and its visible surface, the photosphere, has a temperature of about 5,800 kelvin.
Sunspots are darker, cooler areas of the photosphere. They form where strong magnetic fields slow the flow of heat from below. Their number rises and falls in a cycle of about 11 years.
The Sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion in its core, where hydrogen nuclei join to form helium. The core temperature is about 15 million kelvin.
The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust. It is a main-sequence star and will stay one for several billion years more.

reasons: Rare terms appear in both: spots, rotation in about 25 days, distance in millions of miles.
Sunspot scores well but covers only the spots, not the whole star.

alignments.label: A globe of fire

wikipedia.quote: a nearly perfect sphere of hot plasma

alignments.note: The sun is a hot globe, but nothing in it burns. This is a change in knowledge: the heat comes from fusion, not from a fire.

alignments.label: Size of the sun

britannica.quote: its bulk exceeds that of the earth more than a million of times

wikipedia.quote: Its volume could hold about 1.3 million Earths

alignments.note: The 1810 figure holds. The diameter of 883,000 miles is also close to the modern 864,000 miles.

alignments.label: Distance from the earth
alignments.note: The figure is about 2 percent too large. The transits of Venus gave the right size of the distance, and later methods made it exact.

alignments.label: Rotation in 25 days

britannica.quote: turn round its axis in about 25 days and a half

wikipedia.quote: Its equator turns once in about 25 days

alignments.note: The period holds for the equator. Wikipedia adds that the regions near the poles turn more slowly.

alignments.label: A dark solid body

britannica.quote: a solid opaque body, like the earth, surrounded by a luminous atmosphere

wikipedia.quote: The Sun has no solid surface

alignments.note: This is a change in knowledge. The sun is hot plasma all the way through, with no cool solid body under the light.

alignments.label: What the spots are

britannica.quote: openings in this shining atmosphere, through which we see the dark body of the sun below

wikipedia.quote: Sunspots are darker, cooler areas of the photosphere

alignments.note: The spots are real and do look darker. They are cooler areas made by magnetic fields, not holes that show a dark body.

alignments.label: An inhabited sun

britannica.quote: the body of the sun is inhabited

alignments.note: Wikipedia does not discuss this idea. Inference: the temperature of about 5,800 kelvin at the surface [W5] rules out any life there.

alignments.label: Comets feed the fire

britannica.quote: comets, falling at length into the sun, may serve to recruit its fire

wikipedia.quote: nuclear fusion in its core, where hydrogen nuclei join to form helium

alignments.note: The 1810 entry says the source is not known, which was true then. Comets do not feed the sun; fusion in the core makes its energy.

alignments.label: Age of the sun

wikipedia.quote: The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago

alignments.note: The 1810 entry gives no age. The age comes from later work on radioactivity and on how stars change.

suggestedQuestions: How did the 1810 entry explain the sun's light and heat?
What did Herschel think the sun was made of?
Which 1810 figures for the sun still hold?

How did the 1810 entry explain the sun's.answer: It did not know. It reports Newton's guess that comets fall into the sun and renew its fire [B7]. Wikipedia says the energy comes from nuclear fusion in the core, where hydrogen nuclei join to form helium [W7].

What did Herschel think the sun was made.answer: Herschel took the sun to be a solid dark body inside a luminous atmosphere, and the spots to be openings in that atmosphere [B5]. He even thought the sun might be inhabited [B6]. Wikipedia says the sun has no solid surface and is made of hot plasma [W5], and that the spots are cooler areas made by magnetic fields [W6].

Which 1810 figures for the sun still hol.answer: Its bulk of more than a million earths [B2] fits the modern 1.3 million [W2]. Its rotation of about 25 days [B4] matches the period at the equator [W4]. Its distance of 95 million miles [B3] is a little larger than the modern 93 million [W3].
